metricNote: Artificial Analysis publishes a headline Intelligence Index per model, plus Coding Agent and Agentic indices as separate leaderboards. Per-model sub-index values are not published on the model pages, so every scenario currently gates on the headline index. When a sub-index becomes available per model, switch that scenario's gate.metric and re-anchor its minIndex.
profileNote: Each profile is a typical month of one kind of work: the tokens one request sends and returns, how many requests a month, and how much of the input is a cache read rather than fresh context. The cache share matters as much as the token counts — an agent that resends a stable repo prefix pays the cached rate for most of its input. Every number is an editable starting point, not a measurement; the Recommend view lets you replace all four.

scenarios.label: Daily use
scenarios.description: Questions, summaries, planning, and everyday writing.
scenarios.rationale: About thirteen short exchanges a day. A system prompt and a little recent history are reused; the question itself is new each time.

gate.rationale: Everyday questions still need a model that will not confidently invent an answer, which rules out the small-model tier.

scenarios.label: Easy coding
scenarios.description: Small functions, explanations, tests, and local fixes.
scenarios.rationale: Around seventeen requests a day against one file plus instructions, which get resent across a short back-and-forth, so roughly half the input is a cache read.

gate.rationale: Even a self-contained function has to compile and pass its own test, so the bar sits above the small-model tier.

scenarios.label: Medium coding
scenarios.description: Feature development, refactoring, and multi-file review.
scenarios.rationale: A feature spanning several files at about thirty agent turns a day. The repo context is stable within a session, so most input is a cache read and the output is a tool call rather than an essay.

gate.rationale: Shipping a multi-file feature means holding several files in mind at once; below this bar the edits stop being coherent with each other.

scenarios.label: Hard coding
scenarios.description: Large repos, architectural work, and complex debugging.
scenarios.rationale: Long agent sessions on an unfamiliar large repository, about fifty turns a day. The prefix barely changes between turns, so three quarters of a very large input is billed at the cached rate.

gate.rationale: An unfamiliar large repository punishes weak reasoning quietly, so hard coding admits only the frontier tier.

scenarios.label: Research
scenarios.description: Long documents, literature review, and source analysis.
scenarios.rationale: Roughly seven whole documents a day. Each source is new, so little is cached and the input dominates the bill.

gate.rationale: Holding a long document together and citing it accurately fails quietly rather than loudly, so research sits at the frontier bar.

scenarios.label: Writing
scenarios.description: Drafting, editing, tone adjustment, and long-form copy.
scenarios.rationale: About ten drafting and revision passes a day on one piece. This is the one profile where output rivals input, so output rates decide the bill.

gate.rationale: Copy that ships without a rewrite needs more than fluent text, but it does not need frontier reasoning.

scenarios.label: Innovation
scenarios.description: Brainstorming, strategy, product concepts, and novel ideas.
scenarios.rationale: Around five deliberate thinking sessions a day. A brief and some background are reused, the ideas are not, and answers run long.

gate.rationale: Novel ideation is where frontier capability separates from competence, so innovation admits only the frontier tier.
